4xe-discontinued.text: Stellantis said in January 2026 it would phase out plug-in hybrids in North America starting with the 2026 model year; no 2026 Wrangler 4xe appears in NHTSA recall records.

buy-timing.text: iSeeCars' study of 39M+ used-car sales ranks late November through February as the best odds of a deal and May through early July as the worst; it measures deal odds, not discount size.

crawl-jk-rubicon-auto-410.text: 2012–2018 JK Rubicon automatic (W5A580, 3.59 first) on 4.10 gears with a 4.0:1 case: about 58.9:1 (3.59 × 4.0 × 4.10).

crawl-jl-rubicon-auto-410.text: JL Rubicon automatic on 4.10 gears with the 4.0:1 Rock-Trac case: 77.2:1 crawl ratio.

crawl-jl-rubicon-auto-488.text: JL Rubicon automatic on 4.88 gears: about 91.9:1 (4.71 × 4.0 × 4.88).

curtain-rollover-sensing.note: Owner's manual pp. 245, 252-253 (printed). The manual's silence on rollovers is not a hardware statement; only Stellantis can confirm how the system behaves in a roll.
curtain-rollover-sensing.text: The 2024 owner's manual describes the side curtains as deploying in certain side impacts and lists front and side impact sensors only. It does not mention rollover deployment, describes no switch to turn the side or curtain airbags off, and says nothing about airbags in its doors-off and top-off procedures.

curtains-2018-2023.text: 2018–2023 Wrangler JL has no side-curtain airbags in either row, on any trim or body style (front seat-mounted side airbags only).

curtains-2024-plus.text: From model year 2024, first- and second-row side-curtain airbags are standard on every Wrangler JL trim, 2-door and 4-door, including the 4xe.

curtains-jk.note: Carried from the JL decision research; reverify against a JK owner's manual.
curtains-jk.text: No JK Wrangler (2007–2018) has side-curtain airbags or rear-row airbags; they cannot be retrofitted.

curtains-jt-2024.text: 2024+ Gladiator JT has first- and second-row side-curtain airbags.

front-axle-jl-rubicon.text: The JL Rubicon front axle is the Dana 44 (M210) from 2018 through 2026; the 2024 refresh did not change it.

jk-bumper-on-jl.text: A JK front bumper can be fitted to a 2018–2020 JL with adapter brackets (e.g. DV8 ABJL-01) or drilling and spacers; fit on a 2024 is unconfirmed.

jl-37s-lift.text: Owners run 37-inch tires on JL Rubicons with 2.5–3.5 inch lifts plus rear bump-stop work; long arms pay off mainly above about 4 inches of lift or on 40s.

jl-steering-electric-pump.text: The JL's power-steering pump is electric; owners on 37–38 inch tires locked in 4-Low report overheat warnings and fade.

jl-steering-first.text: On a JL headed for 37s, owners replace the tie rod and drag link (and often the track bar) before the tires go on; the factory parts are called barely adequate for a stock Jeep.

nhtsa-lookup-open-only.text: NHTSA's VIN lookup shows open (unrepaired) recalls only; a clean result does not prove past recall work was done.

ratios-jl-rubicon.text: JL Rubicon comes on 4.10 gears standard with 4.88 optional on the 3.6L; Xtreme Recon uses 4.56; the 392 moved from 3.73 (2021–23) to 4.56 (2024+).

rear-axle-2018-2023-rubicon.text: 2018–2023 JL Rubicon uses a semi-float Dana 44 (M220) rear axle held by C-clips; rear shaft failures on 37-inch tires are a documented owner pattern.

rear-axle-2024-rubicon.text: 2024+ Wrangler Rubicon, Rubicon X and Rubicon 392 use a Dana 44 HD full-float rear axle; no other Wrangler trim gets it.

rear-axle-jt-rubicon.text: 2024 Gladiator Rubicon keeps the semi-float M220 rear axle (window-sticker code DRF), unlike the 2024 Wrangler Rubicon's full-float rear (DRN).

rear-vents-jk.text: JK Wrangler has no rear-seat air outlets.

rear-vents-jlu.text: Owners and press describe rear console air outlets on 4-door JLs, fed by the front HVAC; no manufacturer document found confirms them (Stellantis feature sheets list only rear floor heat ducts).

rubicon-hardware.text: Front and rear Tru-Lok lockers, an electronic front sway-bar disconnect and the 4.0:1 Rock-Trac transfer case are Rubicon-family only, every JL year.

tow-bumper-ball.text: With a ball mounted on the fascia or bumper, any 2026 Wrangler is limited to 3,500 lb and 350 lb tongue weight.

tow-jk-unlimited.text: JK Wrangler Unlimited (4-door) is rated at 3,500 lb.

tow-jl-2018-2023-4door.text: Every 2018–2023 Wrangler JL 4-door is rated 3,500 lb (350 lb tongue weight), Rubicon, diesel and 392 included; every 2-door is rated 2,000 lb.

tow-jl-2024-other-4door.text: Every other 2024–2026 Wrangler 4-door is rated 3,500 lb: the manual Rubicon, a Rubicon on 4.56 or 4.88 gears (including the 35-inch Xtreme 35 package), the 392, every 4xe and the non-Rubicon trims. Every 2-door is rated 2,000 lb.

tow-jl-2024-rubicon-gas-auto.note: The 2024 owner's manual (2nd edition, July 2023) has no Rubicon row and shows 3,500 lb; it predates the March 2024 handbook and the spec sheets. The handbook's tongue-weight conversion next to the 500 lb figure is a copy error (shows 1,587 kg).
tow-jl-2024-rubicon-gas-auto.text: A 2024–2026 4-door Rubicon is rated 5,000 lb (500 lb tongue weight) only as built with the automatic, 4.10 axles and LT285/70R17C 33-inch tires, on the gas 2.0L turbo or 3.6L.

tow-jl-4xe.text: Every Wrangler 4xe is rated 3,500 lb, including the Rubicon 4xe with the full-float rear axle.

tow-jt-rubicon.text: A 2024–2026 Gladiator Rubicon with the automatic and 4.10 axles is rated 7,000 lb; the Sport with the Max Tow package, 7,700 lb. Stellantis doesn't publish tongue weights for these.

tpms-generation.text: TPMS sensors from before mid-2021 don't work on 2022–2024 JLs, so wheels moved from a JK need new sensors.

willys-rear-locker-2024.text: Willys gets a rear locker from model year 2024; 2021–2023 Willys had a Trac-Lok limited slip only.

faq.a: Only 2024 and newer. From model year 2024, first- and second-row side-curtain airbags are standard on every Wrangler JL trim. No JK (2007–2018) and no 2018–2023 JL has curtain airbags in either row, and they can't be added later.
faq.q: Which Jeep Wrangler years have rear-row curtain airbags?

faq.a: The 2024 owner's manual says the side curtains are designed to deploy in certain side impacts and lists front and side impact sensors; it doesn't mention rollover deployment, and it describes no switch to turn the side or curtain airbags off. Its doors-off and top-off procedures don't mention airbags either. That's what the manual documents, not a guarantee about every event, so if an off-camber deployment would rule the Jeep out for you, ask Stellantis directly. The manual also warns against roof changes that could affect the curtains and against aftermarket side steps or body-structure changes.
faq.q: Can the 2024 Wrangler's curtain airbags go off on the trail, and can you turn them off?

faq.a: Wheels and tires (both are 5x5, but plan on new TPMS sensors), the winch, auxiliary lights and loose gear like radios and a Hi-Lift jack. Axles, suspension, steering, armor, the rear bumper, tops and doors don't fit. Some JK front bumpers bolt to a 2018–2020 JL with adapter brackets; fit on a 2024 is unconfirmed.
faq.q: What parts move from a built JK to a JL?

faq.a: It can be. The 2018–2023 Rubicon rear is a semi-float Dana 44 (M220) held by C-clips, and rear shaft failures on 37s are a documented owner pattern. The 2024+ Rubicon, Rubicon X and 392 use a full-float Dana 44 HD rear, which carries the Jeep's weight on the axle tube so the shaft only sees torque.
faq.q: Is the 2018–2023 JL Rubicon rear axle a problem on 37-inch tires?

faq.a: 5,000 lb, but only a 4-door Rubicon with the automatic, 4.10 gears and the factory 33-inch LT285/70R17C tires, on the 2.0L turbo or 3.6L. A manual Rubicon, a Rubicon on 4.56 or 4.88 gears (including the 35-inch Xtreme 35 package), the 392 and every 4xe are rated 3,500 lb, and every 2-door 2,000 lb. The 2024 owner's manual many owners quote shows 3,500 lb because it was printed before the Rubicon row was added. Jeep publishes no rating for a lifted, regeared build, and armor and bigger tires eat into payload and tongue-weight margin.
faq.q: How much can a 2024 Wrangler Rubicon tow?

faq.a: Only if you're comfortable with what's still open. As of October 29, 2026, the battery-fire recall (68C) and the engine casting-sand recall (78C) have remedies available for Wranglers, but the over-the-air power-loss recall (A7C) has only an interim fix and NHTSA's loss-of-power investigation (RQ24-012) is still open. Stellantis said in January 2026 it would drop plug-in hybrids starting with the 2026 model year. If you buy one, check every campaign by VIN, get proof each remedy was done, and confirm the extended battery and engine warranty applies to that vehicle.
faq.q: Should I buy a Wrangler 4xe after the recalls?

faq.a: Late November through February has the best odds of a deal, and May through early July the worst, according to iSeeCars' study of more than 39 million used-car sales. It measures how often deals happen, not how big they are.

recalls.applies: 2021–2025 Wrangler, 4xe included, built June 24, 2020 – Dec 2, 2024 (787,887); also 2021–2025 Gladiator built Aug 18, 2020 – Dec 2, 2024
recalls.owner_instruction: Park away from structures and other vehicles until repaired.
recalls.remedy: Inspect; replace the pump wiring and pump as needed. Available since July 9, 2026.
recalls.title: Power-steering pump connector can overheat and catch fire, even with the ignition off
recalls.verify: Check the VIN, and the door-jamb build date against the June 24, 2020 – Dec 2, 2024 window. Warning signs: lost steering assist or a "Service Power Steering" message.

recalls.applies: 2023–2024 Wrangler built Mar 24 – Jul 27, 2023 (and 2023 Gladiator built Mar 24 – Jul 7, 2023)
recalls.remedy: Inspect and replace the module as needed. Available since May 21, 2024.
recalls.title: Steering column control module weld can stop the driver airbag from deploying

recalls.applies: 2020–2025 Wrangler 4xe built July 1, 2020 – Aug 25, 2025 (228,221 Wranglers; 320,068 including Grand Cherokee 4xe)
recalls.owner_instruction: Don't recharge, and park away from structures and other vehicles, until repaired.
recalls.remedy: Battery analysis and control-module software; the pack is replaced only if trouble codes call for it, with an unlimited-years/miles warranty extension for the defect codes. Vehicles fixed under 95B or B9A still need 68C (nine fires were reported after the 95B fix). Available since Dec 16, 2025.
recalls.title: 4xe high-voltage battery cells can fail internally and catch fire, parked or driving
recalls.verify: Get proof of the 68C remedy itself, not 95B or B9A, and confirm the battery warranty extension applies to this VIN.

recalls.owner_instruction: No parking instruction; a knocking noise or check-engine light can come before failure.
recalls.remedy: Engine computer reflash that detects a pending bearing failure; engine or long block replaced if confirmed, with an extended warranty for the defect. Available for 2024–2025 Wranglers since April 2026. Related: 26E021 covers 2,689 suspect Mopar service engines.
recalls.title: Casting sand in the 2.0L engine can cause bearing failure, loss of drive power or an engine fire (4xe)
recalls.verify: Get proof of the 78C engine software (and any engine replacement) on 2024–2025 builds; listen for knocking on a cold start.

recalls.applies: 2023–2025 Wrangler 4xe built Feb 21, 2023 – June 5, 2025 that received the update (24,238)
recalls.remedy: Interim server-side fix applied to every affected vehicle; the final telematics software update was still being designed as of Stellantis's July 20, 2026 letter.
recalls.title: An over-the-air telematics update can make the hybrid control processor reset and cut drive power (4xe)
recalls.verify: Only an interim fix exists. Ask a dealer whether the final telematics update has been released and applied, and ask the seller about any sudden loss of power.

recalls.remedy: Software changes the failsafe from engine shutdown to limp-home; the filing lists the root cause as unknown.
recalls.title: Lost communication between transmission and hybrid controllers can shut the engine down (4xe)
recalls.verify: Confirm the 22V865 software on 2021–2023 builds, and ask whether the Jeep has ever shut down or gone into limp mode while driving.

recalls.remedy: NHTSA is assessing whether 22V865's scope and remedy are adequate. No outcome yet.
recalls.title: NHTSA investigation into loss of power on the Wrangler 4xe, including vehicles after the 22V865 fix
recalls.verify: No action for an owner yet. Watch for a new recall if NHTSA finds the 22V865 fix inadequate.

recalls.title: Hybrid control software can stop the defroster and defogger from working (4xe)
recalls.verify: Run the defroster before you buy and confirm the windshield starts to clear.

recalls.remedy: Radio software update over the air or at a dealer; owner letters from Sep 2, 2026.
recalls.title: Radio software can stop the rear camera image from showing

recalls.applies: 2026 Wrangler with steel wheels built Nov 10–16, 2025 (606)
recalls.remedy: Dealer inspects and replaces wheels and valve stems.
recalls.title: Steel wheels with walls that may be too thin can crack
